chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liberated Mecca, the men pledged allegiance; then the women came to pledge allegiance to him.

O Holy Prophet, when believing women come to you to pledge allegiance with you not to call anything as partner of Allah, not to steal, not to commit fornication, not to kill their children, not to accuse falsely of their own making, must not disobey you in lawful matters, then pledge allegiance with them and ask forgiveness from Allah for them, Allah is forgiving and merciful.
Hind then said, 'As for the children, we brought them up when they were infants, but we killed them when they grew up.'
Umm Hakim, daughter of al-Harith ibn Hisham, who was with Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is that 'lawful matter' that Allah has commanded us not to disobey you in?'
He replied, 'You must not slap a cheek, abrade a face, pull out hair, tear the front of a shirt, blacken clothes, and you must not cry out woe.'
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pledged allegiance with them on this basis.
She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how can we pledge allegiance to you?'
He said, 'Indeed, I do not place my hand in the hands of women.'
He asked for a bowl of water, immersed his hand, then removed it, and said, 'Immerse your hands in this water,' and that was the pledge of allegiance.

key_terms.تَشْقِيقُ الْجَيْب: Tearing the front of the garment

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad conclude the pledge of allegiance with women without shaking hands?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the specific conditions of the *Bay'at al-Nisa'* (Pledge of Women) revealed in Surah Al-Mumtahanah, highlighting the Prophet's (saww) practical adaptation to avoid physical contact with women while maintaining the spiritual gravity of the covenant. It provides crucial jurisprudential context for Shia scholars regarding the definition of 'goodness' (*ma'ruf*) in marital conduct, as clarified by Hind and Umm Hakim, and establishes the precedent for using water as a medium for the pledge. The narrative underscores the distinct yet equal status of women in the early Islamic community, emphasizing their direct engagement with the Prophet (saww) and the revelation.

en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Aban who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, liberated Makkah men pledged allegiance; then women came to pledge allegiance; and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, said, ‘O Holy prophet, when believing women come to pledge allegiance with you not to call anything as partner of Allah, not to steal, not to commit fornication, not to kill their children, not to accuse falsely of their own making, must not disobey you in lawful matters, then pledge allegiance with them and ask forgiveness from Allah for them, Allah is forgiving and merciful.’ [60:13]
Hind then said, ‘We brought up children from the time they were infants but you killed them when they grew up.’
‘Umm Hakim daughter of al-Harith ibn Hisham, wife of ‘Ikramah ibn abu Jahl asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what is that ‘lawful matters’ that Allah has commanded us not to disobey you?
He (the Messenger of Allah) replied, ‘You must not slap any face, abrade it, pull out any hair, tear apart front part of a shirt, blacken clothes and you must not cry ‘woe is me’.’
The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, pledged allegiance with them on this
and then she said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can we pledge allegiance to you?’
He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘I do not place my hand in the hands of women.’
He (the Messenger of Allah) then asked for a bowl of water and immersed his hand in it and then moved it and told them to immerse their hands in the bowl
